text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
UsedToTrain(x, y) ::: x is used to train y.
TextSummarizationModel(y) ::: y is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) ::: x is a machine learning algorithm.

Premises:
∀x (MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) → (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∃m (TextSummarizationModel(m) ∧ ∃x (MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) ∧ UsedToTrain(x, m))) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃x (Reinforcement(x) ∧ UsedToTrain(x, m)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀x (UsedToTrain(x, m) → RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.

Conclusion:
UsedToTrain(supervised, m) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
